opex.name: Operating, selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the stores, the supply chain and the back office — includes discrete legal and restructuring charges and higher self-insured claims costs.

footerNote: Net profit shown is the $7,026M attributable to Walmart; consolidated net income was $7,151M, after $125M attributable to noncontrolling interests.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: adjusted $0.68, which strips out the investment gain

oneTimers: Other (gains) and losses was a $2,708M gain — mostly fair-value moves on equity investments (a year ago it was a $1,162M loss). Adjusted EPS of $0.68 excludes a $0.26-per-share net gain from these items.

Discrete legal and restructuring charges (about $0.06 per share combined) and a roughly 560-basis-point headwind from higher self-insured general liability claims sit inside operating expenses — they are why reported operating income fell while the adjusted figure rose.
otherDetail: A $2,708M gain on equity and other investments, less $675M of net interest expense. Noncontrolling interests took a $125M share of the profit, which is removed to reach profit attributable to Walmart.

segments.name: Walmart U.S.
segments.note: The big U.S. stores — net sales up 4.8%, comparable sales up 4.6%, with strength in grocery and health & wellness.

segments.name: Walmart International
segments.note: Stores and e-commerce outside the U.S., including Flipkart in India — growth led by China, Walmex and Flipkart.

segments.name: Sam's Club U.S.
segments.note: The warehouse-club business — net sales up 3.4%, membership income up 7.6%.

segments.name: Membership & other income
segments.note: Sam's Club and Walmart membership fees plus advertising — membership income itself grew 15.3% globally.

takeaways.text: Global eCommerce sales grew 25%, led by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery and the marketplace; U.S. store-fulfilled delivery sales grew nearly 50%.
takeaways.title: Online sales keep compounding

takeaways.text: A $2,708M gain on equity and other investments turned an 8.2% drop in operating income into a 56% jump in headline profit, to $7,026M.
takeaways.title: Paper gains lifted the headline

takeaways.text: Operating income fell 8.2% to $7.3B on discrete legal and restructuring charges and higher self-insured general liability claims; on an adjusted, constant-currency basis it rose 0.4%.
takeaways.title: Legal costs and claims hit operations

verdict: Walmart's revenue rose 4.8% to $177.4B with every segment growing — but reported operating profit fell 8.2% to $7.3B on legal and restructuring charges and higher insurance claims, even as a $2.7B investment gain lifted headline profit 56% to $7.0B.
